Filter: draw only some nodes, links or layers

Source: R/mira_filter.R
mira_filter.Rd

Keeps part of the network: some nodes, some links, some layers, or a combination. Each argument takes a condition on the columns of the network's tables, evaluated like subset(): nodes on net$nodes, links on net$extended, layers on net$layers. Variables of your session can be used too. nodes also takes node names, and layers layer names.

Usage

mira_filter(nodes, links, layers)

Arguments

nodes

A condition on the columns of net$nodes (e.g. type == "bird"), or node names. NULL or NA = no node filter.

links

A condition on the columns of net$extended (e.g. weight > 0.05, layer_from == "layer_1"). NULL or NA = no link filter.

layers

A condition on the columns of net$layers (e.g. latitude > -0.6), or layer names. NULL or NA = no layer filter.

Value

A component, to add to a plot with +.

Details

A hidden node hides its links; a hidden layer hides its nodes and links, and the other layers close up the stack. Filters combine: a link is drawn when it passes links, both its nodes pass nodes and both its layers pass layers. A later mira_filter() replaces the same argument of an earlier one, so combine two conditions on nodes in one: nodes = A & B. NULL or NA written in the call removes an earlier filter (mira_filter(nodes = NULL)); a variable that holds NULL is an error.

Rows where a condition is NA are dropped. MiRA shows "Data filter active" with a button that removes the filter. The legends still describe the whole network.

Conditions use the columns as they are named in the tables. On a bipartite network from emln::load_emln() the node sets are in type (nodes = type == "bird"), although MiRA, and mira_options(), call that column node_type.

A condition is evaluated where mira_filter() is called, like subset(): inside a function, it sees that function's variables. A function that passes its arguments on through ... does not see its caller's variables; pass values, not names, through such a wrapper. A node that mira_node(highlight = ) highlights must pass the filter, or MiRA highlights nothing (a warning). MiRA filters in network, grid and map modes; the layer view applies layers only (each bubble stands for a whole layer). In the other views (mira_mode) the whole network is shown, with a warning. The meta-network has its own layer filter, which dims layers instead: mira_mode_meta(layers = ).

See also

mira_intralayer() and mira_interlayer() for min_weight, which hides weak links without a filter.

Other components: mira_camera(), mira_interlayer(), mira_intralayer(), mira_layer(), mira_layout(), mira_legends(), mira_mode, mira_mode_dashboard(), mira_mode_data(), mira_mode_grid(), mira_mode_layer(), mira_mode_map(), mira_mode_meta(), mira_node()

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs
p <- mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.

# Nodes by a condition on their columns
p + mira_filter(nodes = verification_level == "species")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Nodes by name
p + mira_filter(nodes = c("Geospiza_fortis", "Opuntia_echios"))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Links by a condition: strong links, or the links of one layer
p + mira_filter(links = weight > 0.1)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
p + mira_filter(links = layer_from == "layer_1" & layer_to == "layer_1")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Both, in one call; a variable of your session
keep <- c("species", "genus")
p + mira_filter(nodes = verification_level %in% keep, links = weight > 0.05)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Layers by name, or by a condition on net$layers
p + mira_filter(layers = c("layer_1", "layer_3"))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
p + mira_filter(layers = latitude > -0.6)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
